paragraphs: Hyman describes him as a foremost sage of his generation in Babylonia in the time of Rav, and he went up to the Land of Israel. In Hyman’s reading of [Chullin 137b](https://www.sefaria.org/Chullin.137b.12-14), when Issi bar Hini arrived, he found Rabbi Yochanan teaching his son. ([Rashi](https://www.sefaria.org/Rashi_on_Chullin.137b.12.1) there reads: Rabbi Yochanan found Issi bar Hini; and so Ba'ch emended. Hyman suggests that their intention is that Rabbi Yochanan had no sons, as in [Berakhot 5b](https://www.sefaria.org/Berakhot.5b.9) where he said, 'This is the bone of my tenth son,' so how could it say that Rabbi Yochanan was teaching his son? Hyman objects: But this is not much of a proof, for it is possible that his sons grew up enough that he studied with them and afterward they died. Also, the plain sense of the Gemara implies that Issi bar Hini found Rabbi Yochanan studying with his son, not that Rabbi Yochanan found Issi bar Hini, for it does not mention that he had brought with him [כ״ב, unresolved].) The word being taught was “rachelim” (ewes). He said to him: Teach him 'rachelot'. He (Rabbi Yochanan) said to him: As it is written 'rachelim matayim' (two hundred ewes). He said to him: The language of Torah is by itself, and the language of the Sages is by itself. And Rabbi Yochanan asked him: Who is the head of the session in Babylonia? He said to him: Abba Arikha. He (Rabbi Yochanan) said to him: You call him Abba Arikha? (And you did not say 'our teacher,' in a respectful term — [Rashi](https://www.sefaria.org/Rashi_on_Chullin.137b.13.4)). And he asked Rabbi Yochanan: The first of the shearing, at how much? He said to him: At sixty. He said to him: But we learned in a Mishnah: at any amount. Rabbi Yochanan said to him: If so, what is the difference between me and you?

And, as Hyman infers, he afterward went down to Babylonia, as we find in [Shabbat 147a](https://www.sefaria.org/Shabbat.147a.7) [supplied קמז.]: Ulla happened to come to the house of Rasi bar Hini; they asked him (the members of the academy of Asi bar Hini asked Ulla whether one may make a gutter-like fold in a garment on Shabbat; Ulla replied in the name of R. A. [אר״א; named Shabbat 147a: Rabbi Elai]. Hyman criticizes [Seder HaDorot](https://www.girsology.com/seder-hadorot.html?entry=438&lang=en) for giving Ulla as the person who asked Asi).[^7]

And in [Eruvin 39b](https://www.sefaria.org/Eruvin.39b.8): Rav Sheshet said: How can I eat? For Issi taught. Hyman suggests that this is Issi bar Hini, and that he was a reciter (tanna) who taught baraitot.

The supplied קמז. marks147a. The saved named Shabbat147a paragraph concerns garment folds and asks Ulla, not Asi; it explicitly names Rabbi Elai beside the supplied אר״א. The Chullin137b named paragraph has Yochanan finding Issi teaching his son, unlike Hyman’s preferred reading. The full source-specific dispute and כ״ב within the parenthetical argument remain preserved. No children/household guess or twenty-two-ewes reading is introduced.

The actual Rashi on Chullin 137b explicitly takes Rabbi Yochanan as the one who found Issi, and explains the respectful “our teacher” wording. Hyman’s contrary preferred reading and his argument about Yochanan’s sons are preserved as his argument; the reported Bach emendation has not been independently collated. Berakhot 5b supplies the statement about the tenth son without dating the teaching episode. Rashi on Shabbat 147a explains the garment folds; the digital passage names Rabbi Elai. Eruvin 39b has Rav Sheshet ask “How can I eat?”; Hyman’s identification of its Issi with Issi bar Hini remains tentative. The supplied כ״ב, רסי and אר״א forms remain visible and unresolved.

In Hyman’s printed notice (vol. I, p. 240), the abbreviation inside the parenthesis appears as ב״ב, beside supplied כ״ב. The two forms remain distinct and unexpanded. The consulted Rashi on Chullin 137b explicitly has Rabbi Yohanan finding Issi, consistent with the consulted Davidson translation’s division of the dialogue. Hyman favors the other direction of the encounter. The exact Ba’ch apparatus has not been collated.

Hyman’s print gives Asi in the first mention of the household, where the supplied Hebrew has Rasi, and the printed folio reads Shabbat 146a (קמו.). The consulted Shabbat 147a gives Asi, has the people there ask Ulla, and names Rabbi Elai in Ulla’s reply. The consulted Seder HaDorot notice on Issi bar Hini cites 147a and phrases the encounter with Ulla asking him. Hyman’s criticism concerns that direction of the question.

[Chullin 137b:12](https://www.sefaria.org/Chullin.137b.12-14) displays “Rabbi Yochanan” as the subject in its bracketed reading and the consulted English follows that reading. [Rashi](https://www.sefaria.org/Rashi_on_Chullin.137b.12.1) also makes Rabbi Yochanan the one who found Issi. Hyman argues for the reading in which Issi finds Rabbi Yochanan. At [Shabbat 147a:7](https://www.sefaria.org/Shabbat.147a.7) the group asks Ulla, who cites Rabbi Elai. The corresponding [Heilprin entry](https://www.girsology.com/seder-hadorot.html?entry=438&lang=en) makes Ulla the questioner.
